title: Recent Events
bigQuestion: What have you done recently, and what are your plans?
summary: Students learn school-life and future-plans words, talk about recent events with the Present Perfect (already, ever, just, never, yet), give advice and talk about rules with can / could / must / have to / should, and think about making decisions that are right for them.
warmup: What clubs are there at your school?
How do you feel before exams?
What have you done this semester that you are proud of?
What do you want to do when you are a teenager?

grammar.title: Present Perfect with already, ever, just, never, yet
grammar.rule: We use the Present Perfect (have/has + past participle) for things that happened before now when we don't say exactly when. Just means a very short time ago, and already means sooner than expected. Yet goes at the end of questions and negatives, ever is for questions (at any time?), and never means not at any time.
grammar.form: have/has + just / already / never + past participle | Have/Has + subject + ever + past participle? | haven't/hasn't + past participle ... yet
examples: I've just signed up for the gymnastics club.
Sara has already finished her presentation.
Have you ever won a medal?
Omar has never been to Abha.

items.prompt: The bell has ___ rung. Hurry to class!
items.explanation: Just means a very short time ago.

items.prompt: I haven't finished my presentation ___.
items.explanation: Yet goes at the end of negative sentences.

items.prompt: Khalid has ___ been to Abha. He wants to go one day.
items.explanation: Never means not at any time. Khalid hasn't been there.

items.prompt: We've ___ done our homework, so we can play now.
items.explanation: Already means it happened sooner than expected. It goes after have.

items.prompt: ___ you ever been to a gymnastics show?
items.explanation: Present Perfect questions start with Have/Has: Have you ever been ...?

items.prompt: She ___ applied for the scholarship yet.
items.explanation: Use hasn't with she in the Present Perfect.

items.prompt: Sara has just ___ her exam grades.
items.explanation: After has, we use the past participle: seen.

items.prompt: Have you ever ___ a presentation?
items.explanation: The past participle of give is given.

items.prompt: Nouf has just ___ up for the athletics club.
items.explanation: Sign is regular, so the past participle is signed.

items.prompt: We haven't ___ our exam grades yet.
items.explanation: The past participle of get is gotten (American English) or got.

items.prompt: Khalid has never ___ a machine before.
items.explanation: Invent is regular: invented.

items.prompt: Has Reem ___ for the scholarship yet?
items.explanation: Apply ends in consonant + y, so we change y to i: applied.

items.prompt: I've already ___ my classmates about the trip.
items.explanation: The past participle of tell is told.

items.prompt: My cousin has ___ graduated! The party is today.
items.explanation: Just means a very short time ago. Yet and ever don't go here.

items.prompt: Have you decided what to do next semester ___?
items.explanation: Yet goes at the end of questions.
Have + you + ever + past participle?

items.answer: I have just signed up for athletics.
items.explanation: have + just + past participle.

items.answer: We haven't decided what to do yet.
alt: We haven't yet decided what to do.
items.explanation: Yet usually goes at the end of a negative sentence.

items.answer: She has already finished her presentation.
alt: She has finished her presentation already.
items.explanation: Already usually goes between has and the past participle.

items.answer: My brother has never failed an exam.
items.explanation: has + never + past participle.

items.prompt: Omar has finished his presentation.
answer: Omar hasn't finished his presentation yet.
Omar has not finished his presentation yet.
items.explanation: hasn't + past participle ... yet.

items.prompt: You have won a medal.
answer: Have you ever won a medal?
items.explanation: Have + you + ever + past participle?

items.prompt: The semester has ended.
items.explanation: Just goes between has and the past participle.

items.prompt: Sara has applied for the course.
answer: Has Sara applied for the course yet?
items.explanation: Has + subject + past participle ... yet?

answer: I have never seen that advertisement.

After have, use the past participle: decided.

items.sentence: Have you ever been to a gymnastics show?

items.explanation: Correct: Have + you + ever + been.
Correct: hasn't + past participle + yet.

grammar.title: Modal verbs: can, could, must, have to, should
grammar.rule: Can is for ability or for something that is possible. Could is for an idea or suggestion. Must is for something you think is very important to do, have to is for a rule from someone else, and should is for advice. After can, could, must and should, use the base verb with no to and no -s. Have to changes with he/she/it: has to.
grammar.form: subject + can / could / must / should + base verb | subject + have to / has to + base verb
examples: You could look on the school website.
I must study for my exams.
We have to wear a uniform at school.
You should apply for the scholarship.

items.prompt: Fahad ___ swim very fast.
items.explanation: Can never takes -s or to: Fahad can swim.

items.prompt: She ___ apply for the scholarship before Friday.
items.explanation: With she, have to becomes has to.

items.prompt: You should ___ for your exams.
items.explanation: After should, use the base verb with no to.

items.prompt: Do we ___ wear sneakers for athletics?
items.explanation: Questions with do use have to: Do we have to ...?

items.prompt: Which sentence gives advice?
options: You should ask your teacher for help.
You have to wear a uniform.
items.answer: You should ask your teacher for help.
items.explanation: We use should to give advice.

items.prompt: Which sentence is about ability?
items.explanation: Can tells us what someone is able to do.

items.prompt: Which sentence talks about a rule from someone else?
options: We have to be at school by 7 a.m.
We could go to the park.
items.answer: We have to be at school by 7 a.m.
items.explanation: Have to is for rules from outside, like school rules.

items.prompt: Khalid is good at gymnastics. He ___ do a handstand.
items.explanation: Can is for ability.

items.prompt: We ___ to finish our presentation by Sunday. The teacher said so.
items.explanation: Only have goes before to: have to is a rule from the teacher.

items.prompt: You look tired. You ___ go to bed early tonight.
items.explanation: Should is for advice. Has to doesn't go with you.

items.prompt: "What can we do this weekend?" "We ___ visit the science museum!"
items.explanation: Could is for an idea or suggestion.

items.prompt: I ___ remember to call my grandmother. I promised her!
items.explanation: Must is for something you feel is very important to do.

items.prompt: Sara ___ come to the club today because she needs to study for an exam.
items.explanation: Can't means it isn't possible for her today.

items.prompt: Does Omar ___ wear a tracksuit for athletics?
items.explanation: After does, use have to (not has to).

items.answer: You should try to improve your grades.
items.explanation: should + base verb (try).

items.answer: We have to wear a uniform.
items.explanation: have to + base verb (wear).

items.answer: You could join the gymnastics club.
items.explanation: could + base verb for a suggestion.

items.answer: I must finish my application today.
alt: Today I must finish my application.
items.explanation: must + base verb (finish).

items.answer: Can you help me with my presentation?
items.explanation: Questions with can: Can + subject + base verb?

items.prompt: Sara must wear a uniform. (It's a school rule.)
answer: Sara has to wear a uniform.
items.explanation: For a rule from outside, use has to with she.

items.prompt: You should believe every advertisement.
answer: You should not believe every advertisement.
items.explanation: Add not after should: shouldn't.

items.prompt: Reem can speak French.
items.explanation: Put can before the subject.

items.prompt: We have to sign up today.
answer: Do we have to sign up today?
items.explanation: Questions with have to use do: Do we have to ...?

items.instruction: Make a suggestion with could. Start with: You could ...
items.prompt: Why don't you ask your classmate for help?
answer: You could ask your classmate for help.
items.explanation: could + base verb gives a suggestion.

items.sentence: You should to study for the exams.
items.answer: You should study for the exams.
items.explanation: No to after should.

items.sentence: He have to apply before Monday.
items.answer: He has to apply before Monday.
items.explanation: With he, use has to.

items.sentence: We must keep our classroom clean.
items.answer: We must keep our classroom clean.
items.explanation: Correct: must + base verb.

items.sentence: Do I must sign up online?
items.answer: Do I have to sign up online?
items.explanation: We don't use do with must. Use Do I have to ...?
Can never takes -s.

items.sentence: You could ask the assistant in the library.
items.answer: You could ask the assistant in the library.
items.explanation: Correct: could + base verb for a suggestion.

reading.title: Reem's Choice
reading.text:
It was the first week of the new semester, and there was a big advertisement on the school wall: Sign up for a club! Reem's best friends, Nouf and Sara, ran to the athletics table. "Come on, Reem! We've already signed up," Nouf said.

Reem looked at the athletics table. Then she looked at the table next to it. It said Young Inventors Club. A teacher was showing a small robot that could clean a desk. Reem's eyes opened wide.

"I've never been good at running," she thought. "But I've always wanted to invent things." She felt worried. Her friends wanted her to join athletics with them.

Reem took a deep breath. She walked to the inventors' table and wrote her name. Then she went back to her friends. "I'm sorry," she said. "I've decided to join the inventors' club instead."

Sara smiled. "That's great! You should do what you love." Nouf agreed. "And you can invent a robot that carries our bags after athletics!"

Two months later, Reem gave a presentation about her first invention. Her friends sat in the front row and clapped the loudest.

questions.explanation: She said, "I've decided to join the inventors' club instead."

questions.explanation: She showed her first invention, and her friends clapped the loudest.

reading.title: News from Riyadh
reading.text:
Hi Yousef,

How are you? It's been a long time since you moved to Dammam! I miss playing football with you after school. Here is my news.

We've just finished our exams. I was worried about math, but I got a great grade! My classmates and I made a study group, and it really helped me improve.

Guess what? I've signed up for the gymnastics club. I've never done gymnastics before, so I fall a lot! Our coach says I have to practice every day.

I've also applied to be an assistant in the school library. I had to fill out an application and talk to the librarian. I haven't heard back yet, but I hope I get it. I love books, and the library has several new science magazines.

My big brother is a teenager now. He wants to get a scholarship to study engineering. He says he wants to invent a car that runs on sunlight!

What about you? Have you joined any clubs yet? Do you like your new school? You should send me some photos!

Write back soon,
Khalid

reading.title: The Girl Who Invented a Smart Bottle
reading.text:
Our school magazine has just interviewed Sara from Grade 6. She has invented a water bottle that reminds you to drink.

Q: Congratulations, Sara! What exactly have you invented?
A: Thank you! I've invented a smart bottle. It has a small light. If you don't drink for one hour, the light turns on.

Q: Why did you decide to make it?
A: Last summer, my little brother got sick because he didn't drink enough water. I wanted to help him.

Q: Have you ever invented anything before?
A: No, never! This is my first invention. But I've always been interested in science.

Q: Was it difficult?
A: Yes, very! I've made several bottles, and the first three didn't work. My teacher said I should keep trying. Each time, I could improve something small.

Q: Have you shown it to your classmates yet?
A: Yes, I've already given a presentation in class. Everyone wanted one!

Q: What advice can you give other students?
A: You don't have to be a genius. You must be patient, and you should never give up.

Q: What's next?
A: I haven't decided yet. Maybe a bottle that can talk!

options: It turns on a light if you don't drink for an hour.
It keeps water cold all day.
It plays music when it is empty.

questions.explanation: Sara says that if you don't drink for one hour, the light turns on.

She wanted to win a scholarship.

questions.explanation: She says, "I've already given a presentation in class."

questions.explanation: Sara says, "My teacher said I should keep trying."

questions.prompt: Which sentence from the interview gives advice?
questions.explanation: We use should for advice, and Sara gives this advice to other students.

reading.title: My Brother's Big Dream
reading.text:
Hi everyone! It's Fahad again. Today I want to tell you about my big brother, Nasser.

Nasser is a teenager. He's eighteen, and he has just graduated from high school. My whole family went to his graduation. Mom cried, and Dad took about a hundred photos!

Nasser has always been interested in medicine. He wants to be a doctor and help people in our town. Last month, he saw an advertisement for a scholarship at a university in Jeddah. He decided to apply.

The application was long. He had to write about himself and send his grades. He also had to get two letters from his teachers. He worked on it every night for two weeks. I helped him a little. I made him tea!

Nasser has already sent his application, but he hasn't heard back yet. He checks his e-mail about twenty times a day. Mom says he should relax, but he can't.

I've never seen my brother so nervous. I'm nervous too! If he gets the scholarship, he will have to move to Jeddah. I'll miss him, but I know he can do it.

Have you ever applied for something important? Leave a comment below!

reading.title: End of Semester News
reading.text:
Al-Yasmin Girls' School, Abha

What a busy semester it has been! Here is the latest news from Grade 6.

Exams: The students have just finished their final exams. Well done, girls! Your grades will be ready next Sunday. You can see them online.

Gymnastics: Our gymnastics team has won second place in the Abha schools' competition. They have practiced three times a week since September. Lama and Reem have never competed before, but they were amazing!

The school garden: Grade 6 has already planted several trees behind the library. But we haven't finished the flower beds yet, and we need help! Students who are interested can sign up with Ms. Amal, our science assistant.

Athletics Day: Athletics Day was on Thursday, but it rained, so we had a quiz in the hall instead. We will have the races next month.

Reminders: All students must bring their library books back by Wednesday. You have to return them before the holiday. And remember, you should read at least one book over the break!

Have a great holiday, everyone!

wordWork.title: Categorizing words: verbs, nouns and adjectives
wordWork.rule: Many verbs have a noun in the same word family. We often add -ion, -ation or -ment: decide → decision, apply → application, improve → improvement. Adjectives with -ed tell how a person feels (interested); adjectives with -ing describe the thing (interesting).

items.prompt: Which word is a noun?
items.explanation: Application is a thing (a form), so it is a noun.

items.prompt: Which word is a verb?
items.explanation: Invent is an action, so it is a verb.

items.prompt: Verb: apply → Noun: ___
items.explanation: apply → application (y changes to i, then add -cation).

items.prompt: Verb: improve → Noun: ___
items.explanation: Add -ment: improve → improvement.

items.prompt: Verb: decide → Noun: ___
items.explanation: decide → decision (take away -de and add -sion).

items.prompt: Verb: invent → Noun: ___
items.explanation: Add -ion: invent → invention.

items.prompt: I'm ___ in gymnastics. I want to join the club.
items.explanation: Use -ed for how a person feels: I'm interested.

items.prompt: That was a very ___ presentation about space!
items.explanation: Use -ing to describe the thing: an interesting presentation.

items.prompt: "Reem gave a great presentation." What type of word is presentation?
items.explanation: Presentation is a thing Reem gave, so it is a noun.

items.prompt: Which group has only verbs?
items.explanation: Decide, follow and keep are all actions.

writing.prompt: Write an e-mail to catch up with an old friend.
writing.hint: Talk about exams, clubs and plans. Use: I've just ..., I've already ..., I haven't ... yet, I've never ..., Have you ever ...?
writing.model:
Hi Sara,

How have you been? I've just finished my exams, and I got good grades in English and science! I've already signed up for the art club for next semester. I've never painted with oils before, so I'm excited. I haven't decided about the summer course yet. Have you ever been to a summer course? Write back soon!
